conviction_note: The bar ($1.31-1.32 consensus) sits on the midpoint of the company's own H2 guide, and Q2's $1.41 core run-rate points to a small beat. Against that, a Fed hike on 2026-09-16 and a peer's 6bp rise in deposit costs threaten the Q4 margin guide, and a GAAP headline carrying Lincoln deal costs is a small negative. The evidence is balanced: p_up 50 on a 2.5% absolute scale, and the findings sum to 0.0. The scale is the 1.76% median reaction, raised for the hunters' known undersizing and for the -6.63% tail when Q2 2025 missed.
bar: Q3 2026 core diluted EPS $1.31 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EQBK/earnings-forecasts) and $1.32 (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/EQBK). Tickflow shows a $1.27 mean of 3 analysts (https://tickflow.io/stock/EQBK/forecast). The bar agrees with the company's H2 2026 guide: NIM 4.25-4.35%, average earning assets $6.85-6.95bn, non-interest income $18-22m for H2, non-interest expense $94-98m for H2 (Q2 8-K ex-99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227500/000119312526303176/eqbk-ex99_1.htm). At the guide midpoints, with ~$2m provision, a 22% tax rate and 20.6m shares, that arithmetic gives about $1.30-1.33. Revenue consensus is about $85-86m.
positioning_check: Short interest 591,717 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, ~2.9% of 20.59m shares outstanding, 5.48 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/eqbk/short-interest, read 2026-10-14 by the sweep). Not crowded. The options chain is unusable (ATM spread 186% of mid, OI 288, put/call OI 0.06), so there is no skew. Spot $46.01 is -6.5% over 20 days and -11% from the 52-week high, and below the $49.85 reference price of the Lincoln deal on 2026-09-02. Analyst targets $47-59 (Stephens raised to $59 on 2026-07-16).

findings.finding: Q2 2026 core EPS was $1.41 (GAAP $1.27), with core non-interest expense of $46.8m and NIM 4.36%. The Q3 consensus of $1.31-1.32 assumes expenses rising to the $47-49m/quarter guide and NIM easing toward the 4.30% midpoint. If expenses and NIM hold near Q2 levels, core EPS lands around $1.36-1.40, a 3-6% beat. This sits inside what the company guided, and loans fell $22.6m in Q2, which caps the upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: core $1.41 vs ~$1.24-1.32 consensus, a beat, and the stock moved +0.47%. Q3 2025: core $1.21 beat, despite a GAAP loss from bond repositioning, -1.85%. Q2 2025: missed (core $0.94, revenue -3.4% vs estimates), -11% after hours and -6.63% at the close. Beats are bought weakly; misses are punished.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus sits on the guided midpoint rather than the Q2 run-rate. If the market expected the run-rate, estimates would be near $1.38-1.40 rather than $1.31. But this is a guided-range item and three to nine analysts can do the same arithmetic.
findings.independence: Consensus figures come from Benzinga and Earnings Whispers (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EQBK/earnings-forecasts). The Q2 run-rate and the guide come from the same 8-K, so they are one document.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, a 12-0 vote. The first calendar-Q3 regional bank print, FB Financial on 2026-10-13, showed the cost of interest-bearing deposits up 7bp to 2.88% and NIM down 12bp to 3.83%, on funding costs. EQBK raised brokered deposits from 5.7% to 8.0% of deposits in Q2 and guided NIM down to 4.25-4.35%. Funding-cost pressure is a risk to the Q3 margin and to the Q4 NIM outlook on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM has been the headline line. Q2 2026 (NIM +3bp to 4.36%) moved +0.47%, and Q2 2025 (margin expansion but a revenue miss) moved -6.63%. There is no prior print with a NIM guide cut on record.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. EQBK is -6.5% over 20 days, which covers the hike. It is a proxy: EQBK's loan production yields 6.56% and the company may be asset-sensitive, so a hike could help asset yields. Had the market fully priced a margin cut, sell-side Q3 numbers would sit below the guide midpoint, and they do not.
findings.independence: The Fed statement (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm) is a separate document. It is still a proxy: the company has not confirmed any funding-cost pressure.

findings.finding: The Lincoln Bancorp merger, signed 2026-09-02 (~$123.8m, 77.5% stock), and the S-4 filed 2026-10-05 mean Q3 GAAP EPS will carry merger expenses (Q1 2026 carried $5.7m). The wire headline will likely print GAAP below core, as in Q3 2025 when GAAP was a loss. The call is also the first Q&A on the deal: tangible book dilution, earnback under 3 years, a 5.1% 2027 EPS accretion claim.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: GAAP loss from merger costs and bond repositioning, core beat, -1.85%. Q1 2026: $5.7m merger expenses, GAAP $0.80, -2.52% (cause not isolated).
findings.why_not_priced: The deal costs are known, and core EPS strips them out. The only unpriced part is the headline-print mechanics on a thinly traded name, so the finding is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Retail Banker International on the deal metrics (https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/news/equity-bancshares-and-lincoln-bancorp-agree-123-8m-merger/); the S-4 index (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1227500/000119312526412874/).

findings.finding: The board raised the quarterly dividend 22%, from $0.18 to $0.22, declared 2026-09-10. A raise inside the quarter is a signal of management confidence in run-rate earnings into the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction isolated to a dividend line.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is a public 8-K. The stock fell after the raise, so the market did not treat it as an earnings signal.
findings.independence: Repeated in Lincoln's shareholder letter, Form 425 of 2026-09-22 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1227500/000119312526398104/d20635d425.htm).

findings.finding: A new 1,000,000-share buyback (~4.9% of shares) received Fed non-objection on 2026-08-05 and starts when the old plan is used up or on 2026-09-30. The old plan had 116,293 shares left after Q2. At $46 vs TBV $33.45 (1.38x), Q3/Q4 repurchases are possible, but a pending stock-funded merger may restrict them during the proxy period.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 bought back 211,369 shares at $45.02; that print moved +0.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public 8-K. Pace commentary on the call is the only new information, and it could be zero if buybacks are paused for the deal.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K buyback figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227500/000119312526303176/eqbk-ex99_1.htm), the same company source.

findings.finding: Nonperforming assets rose to $66.3m (0.86% of assets) from $58.4m (0.76%) in Q2, from additions in the acquired Frontier portfolio. ACL is 1.19% of loans (1.73% with purchase discounts) and classified assets are 11.9% of capital. Peer FB Financial's Q3 showed benign credit (NCOs 0.04%, NPAs flat at 1.13%), which offsets part of the risk of further migration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 provision of $6.0m (Frontier reserve build) coincided with -2.52%. Q2 2026 provision of $1.3m: +0.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: The trend is public. Only the Q3 direction is unknown. Purchase discounts give an extra cushion beyond the ACL.
findings.independence: FB Financial Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000063/a3q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm) points the other way, toward benign credit.

outside_window.finding: Lincoln Bancorp merger close, expected in Q4 2026 and subject to Lincoln shareholder and regulatory approval. It projects 5.1% 2027 EPS accretion and ~$9.1bn of total assets.

baseline_tension: No usable skew. The -6.5% 20-day run-up and the discount to the $49.85 deal price fit a market already pricing rate and funding pressure, which leaves the modest run-rate beat case as the less-priced side. The two offset, and the result is balanced.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the run-rate beat finding lands inside the H2 guide, so it was cut from +0.4 to +0.3; the bar has two agreeing sources ($1.31/$1.32) plus the guide, so there is no cap
Lesson 5 (proxy): the Fed hike and peer deposit-cost finding is unconfirmed by the company, so it was cut from -0.4 to -0.3
Lesson 2 (one-off): the GAAP merger-cost headline was cut from -0.2 to -0.1 as below-the-line with no path to the guide
Lessons 7 and 8 checked: short interest is not crowded and no confirmed unpriced company number exists, so no resize
